answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by staking reputation to a verifiable cost: before an agent may trade, it locks a small bond released only after it completes real work vouched for by independent peers. Like a river filling a harbor through one guarded channel, all trust must flow through one attested identity. Building ten fakes costs ten bonds plus ten proofs of work, while an honest agent's crystal-clear history compounds into cheaper, higher-value trading rights. Attackers pay per identity; the honest pay once.
